presenceCondition:
(and (= CONFIG_LOCKDEP true)
     (= CONFIG_SLOB true)
     (= CONFIG_PPC_256K_PAGES false)
     (= CONFIG_SLAB true)
     (= CONFIG_FORCE_MAX_ZONEORDER false))
model:
(define-fun CONFIG_SLAB () Bool
  true)
(define-fun CONFIG_SLOB () Bool
  true)
(define-fun CONFIG_PPC_256K_PAGES () Bool
  false)
(define-fun CONFIG_LOCKDEP () Bool
  true)
(define-fun CONFIG_FORCE_MAX_ZONEORDER () Bool
  false)
reasoning: TRUE POSITIVE (OVER-CONSTRAINED): Same bug as PRODUCT_108/135 (0f8f8094d28.c, Linux kmalloc). Line 36 accesses kmalloc_caches[i] inside #ifdef CONFIG_LOCKDEP, but kmalloc_caches is declared inside #ifndef CONFIG_SLOB. When SLOB=true, kmalloc_caches is undeclared and the tool detects accessing it as PULSE_UNINITIALIZED_VALUE on 'cache'. This is the known vbdb OutOfBoundsRead/UndeclaredIdentifier bug. OVER-CONSTRAINED: The core condition is LOCKDEP=true && SLOB=true; SLAB=true is both unnecessary and contradictory (SLOB and SLAB are mutually exclusive in Linux). The presence condition also includes PPC_256K_PAGES=false and FORCE_MAX_ZONEORDER=false which are irrelevant to the bug.
